sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling with a randomized finite-support instrument conditional on each finite covariate stratum.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional multinomial cell probabilities are empirical within \((x,z)\); finite-sample inversion uses cellwise Clopper--Pearson intervals and asymptotics use their multinomial influence vectors.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper learns deterministic categorical rules by minimizing a loss formed from coordinatewise action-mean intervals and explicitly leaves randomized rules for future development.
Proposition 1 characterizes all minimax allocations when every action-specific spike state is feasible.
Theorems 2 and 3 establish local asymptotic minimaxity of an empirical-success statistical treatment rule with many point-identified treatments under an asymptotically balanced sampling design.

Theorem 5.1 gives a binary stochastic policy whose treatment probability is formed from lower and upper bounds on a conditional treatment-effect contrast and improves the deterministic worst-case-regret bound.

body.tldr: For the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, the paper identifies the full joint action-mean polytope and solves the resulting randomized minimax-regret game. Its inferential conclusion is a sharp regular--irregular dichotomy: on separated nondegenerate unique faces, the moving-coefficient KKT map is Hadamard differentiable and admits a uniform root-\(n\) Gaussian law; at intersections of optimal faces, no uniformly honest random closed set can contract to the exact optimizer correspondence at any vanishing rate, so uniform consistency itself fails there. The exact Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson confidence-fiber union remains uniformly valid at those intersections, but it is deliberately noncontracting there. Pure-rule certificates, the spike-state specialization, the exact three-action joint-versus-rectangle witness, and deployed-regret certification complete the decision analysis.

project_justification.gap: Song et al.'s model M1 supplies the compatible response-law restrictions for discrete instruments and outcomes, but it does not provide randomized minimax-regret optimization or sampling inference for the resulting optimizer correspondence. Existing random-linear-program theory generally fixes constraint normals, while here the observable multinomial table changes both the feasible response bases and the active regret coefficients. The unresolved inferential issue was therefore not merely differentiability on a regular face, but whether any uniformly honest contraction can survive intersections of optimal faces.
project_justification.niche: The paper studies the binary-outcome, finite-covariate-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s M1 and links response-type partial identification to a finite randomized saddle program. It separates regular laws, where observable basis, slack, reduced-cost, and active-face margins stabilize the KKT system and yield root-\(n\) Gaussian inference, from irregular face intersections, where locally indistinguishable laws force a fixed optimizer-set error and preclude contraction at every vanishing rate.
project_justification.fill: The positive result gives the explicit moving-coefficient derivative and uniform Gaussian policy-and-value law on separated nondegenerate unique faces. The negative result gives an explicit full-compliance local submodel proving that no data-based random closed set can combine uniform asymptotic coverage with contraction at any vanishing rate at face intersections; in particular, neither uniform consistency nor uniform root-\(n\) contraction is possible. Exact finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage is the valid noncontracting fallback. The rectangle-safety counterexample also applies to Hruza et al.'s broader overlapping bound-agnostic class by inclusion, but the positive sampling and KKT theorem is proved only for this paper's narrower response-type model and does not transfer by that inclusion.

body.related_work: Manski2000TreatmentChoice separates treatment choice from point identification, and Stoye2007ManyTreatments supplies the spike-state population allocation benchmark recovered here when every spike is feasible. Masten2023ManyTreatmentRules studies a different repeated-sample treatment-choice problem. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Asymptotics develops local-Gaussian decision rules for randomized partial-identification minimax regret when bounds shrink at the root-\(n\) scale. That decision-theory result neither constructs the fixed-law response-type joint-polytope optimizer correspondence nor supplies honest set inference that contracts across its face intersections; it therefore neither supplies nor contradicts the fixed-error impossibility proved here. Conversely, the present fixed-law correspondence result does not claim their local asymptotic minimaxity. Cui2021PartialIDDecisions randomizes a binary action from marginal contrast bounds; it does not optimize three or more actions against a joint categorical-instrument response polytope. SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV supplies model M1's response-law compatibility restrictions; the present model is its binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization, not a claim about all of models M1--M5. SachsEtAl2023SymbolicBounds and MastinJailletChin2014RandomizedRegret provide the response-function linear-program and finite saddle ingredients, whose composition is treated as background. HruzaEtAl2026CategoricalPIL studies a broader, overlapping bound-agnostic class and a coordinatewise-interval decision rule. Inclusion carries the paper's negative rectangle-safety witness to that broader class, but it does not carry the positive response-basis, KKT, or Gaussian theorem. BonnansShapiro2000Perturbation informs the separated-face analysis; KlattMunkZemel2022RandomLP and LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023LPConfidence concern fixed-coefficient formulations that do not cover the moving active normals here. FangSantos2019DirectionalInference motivates derivative-aware inference at nonsmooth maps, while the theorem here proves the stronger obstruction that a uniformly honest random closed set cannot contract at any vanishing rate to the exact optimizer set at face intersections, and hence cannot be uniformly consistent there. ClopperPearson1934Binomial and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007Sets inform the exact, noncontracting confidence-fiber fallback.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The Gaussian policy-and-regret law is restricted to the observable nondegenerate unique-face class with fixed-support, response-basis, rank, slack, reduced-cost, and active-weight margins. At face intersections, the impossibility theorem rules out every uniformly honest vanishing-rate contraction to the exact optimizer correspondence, including uniform consistency and uniform root-\(n\) contraction; the Bonferroni confidence-fiber union remains valid but can be conservative and noncontracting. The negative rectangle-safety witness transfers to broader classes containing the displayed law, including the overlapping Hruza et al. class, but the positive active-basis and KKT theory requires this paper's response-type structure and stated margins.
body.honest_scope: The maintained causal model is the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, with finite randomized instrument support, categorical treatment, response-type exogeneity, consistency, exclusion, positive stratum--instrument support, and response-fiber compatibility. The response-function projection and its composition with a finite randomized-regret linear program are background ingredients. Uniform root-\(n\) Gaussian inference is proved only on the separated nondegenerate unique-face class; it is not claimed at face intersections. At those intersections, an explicit full-compliance local submodel proves that every uniformly honest random closed set must forgo contraction at every vanishing rate to the exact optimizer correspondence, so even uniform consistency is impossible unless a population face is selected or the target is weakened to a local outer limit. The exact Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson confidence-fiber set remains finite-sample valid without a contraction claim. Hruza et al.'s class is broader and overlapping rather than identical: only the negative rectangle-safety counterexample transfers upward by inclusion, while the positive sampling and KKT theorem does not.
